slides.original_header: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. (NSE: SUNPHARMA) is India's largest pharma company and the largest Indian player in the US market. FY26 consolidated revenue grew 11.9% YoY to ~₹58,220 crore, EBITDA rose 16.1% to ~₹17,700 crore, and net profit grew 5% to ~₹11,479 crore. Stock trades at ~₹1,880–1,900 (market cap ~₹4.6 lakh crore, mid-July 2026), 52-week range ₹1,548–1,963, P/E ~38–39x, near debt-free, dividend payout ~34%.

slides.original_header: Sun Pharma recorded a net cash outflow of ₹5,306 crore from investing activities in FY25, mainly driven by capital expenditure of ₹2,068 crore towards manufacturing capacity and R&D infrastructure, alongside net investment purchases (largely mutual funds and other financial instruments) of ₹3,864 crore. Capex has stayed in the ₹1,000–3,200 crore range through the period, with FY19 seeing the highest spend at ₹3,162 crore, reflecting continued but disciplined reinvestment even as the business scaled. Investing outflows have also included acquisitions of subsidiaries in select years, most notably FY23 (₹4,686 crore) and FY25, supporting Sun Pharma's push into specialty and global branded generics. A few years, like FY21 and FY24, saw comparatively modest net outflows as investment sales and maturing deposits partly offset fresh deployments, underscoring an investing strategy that balances growth spending with liquidity management.

slides.original_header: The ROE of Sun Pharma has remained resilient over the last decade, recovering from a low of 5.60% in FY18 to 14.74% in FY26. This improvement reflects stronger shareholder value creation, supported primarily by expanding profitability, improving asset utilization, and disciplined capital allocation following the successful scale-up of the Global Specialty business. The improvement in ROE has been driven by a steady increase in the Asset Turnover Ratio, which improved from 0.42x in FY18 to 0.58x in FY26, indicating more efficient utilization of assets to generate revenue. At the same time, the Net Profit Margin strengthened significantly from 7.90% in FY18 to 19.72% in FY26, reflecting higher profitability driven by an improved product mix and operational efficiency. Financial Leverage has steadily declined from 1.99x in FY16 to 1.29x in FY26, highlighting the company's conservative capital structure and lower dependence on debt. Despite lower leverage, Sun Pharma has continued to deliver healthy equity returns, demonstrating that profitability growth rather than financial leverage has been the key driver of ROE. The Capital Turnover Ratio improved from 0.53x in FY18 to 0.72x in FY26, while EBIT Margin expanded from 15.09% to 28.92% during the same period. Consequently, ROCE increased from 7.98% in FY18 to 20.70% in FY26, reflecting significantly better capital utilization and reinforcing management's ability to generate stronger returns on invested capital.
